page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with paragraphs numbered in Roman numerals (XXII to XXVI). No margin notes. Bottom: catchword at the right and gathering signature at the centre-left. Faint show-through from the reverse side is visible and not transcribed.

main_text.l: XXII.
Discernatur etiam summum ius ab æquita-
te. Etsi enim genere congruunt, quia utroq; pro-
bantur recta & damnantur contraria, tamen
gradibus differunt propter circumstantia-
s.
XXIII.
Est igitur summum ius cum leges seuere sine
mitigatione retinentur, etiam cum propter cir-
cumstantiam aliquam probabilis ratio erat mi-
tigationis.
XXIIII.
ἐπιεικεια[?] vero seu æquitas est probabilis mi-
tigatio summi iuris in aliqua circumstantia, pr-
æsertim in casu, de quo non principaliter lex lo-
quitur.
XXV.
Et quoniam ἐπιεικεια[?] aut publica est, aut priuata,
publicam illam quæ in iudiciis versatur
Magistratibus & Iurisconsultis relinquamus,
qui sapientissime disputant, utrum iudicandum
sit ex scripto iure, an æquitas extra scriptum
quærenda sit, priuatam vero, cuius tres sunt gra-
dus, nisi exercebimus, nihil dilectioni erga pro-
ximum relinquemus.
XXVI.
Primus gradus est eleganter ferre commu-
nes hominum infirmitates, quæ non puniuntur legi[?]bus.
De hoc gradu Plinius dixit: Qui vitia odit,
homines odit. Nemo enim sine vitiis nascitur

page.notes: The last paragraph (from "Primus gradus" to "nascitur") is struck through with ink lines in the scan; the text is still printed and is transcribed in full. The Greek word ἐπιεικεια is faint and uncertain in both places. "legibus" is partly obscured by the strike-through. A faint word "Dicer" at the lower left looks like show-through or a stray mark and is not transcribed. A stain in the left margin beside XXII is not text. The page has no printed page number or running head; "A 5" is the gathering signature.
